name: Vaishali
why_it_matters: Krishna Adiga's 75-year-old Udupi-Maharashtrian anchor on FC Road — SPDP is the city's afternoon snack default, a fried-flour basket holding dahi, spud-wedge, tamarind, sev. Generations of Pune students have stood in the same queue.
insider_tip: SPDP runs out by 4.30pm — order with the first round. Sabudana khichdi only Monday + Thursday mornings (vrat days). Cash + UPI, no cards. Queue 12-2pm + 7-9pm; arrive 11am or after 3pm for no-wait.
signature_address: 1218/1, Fergusson College Road, Shivaji Nagar, Pune 411004

name: Bedekar Misal
why_it_matters: Vinayak Hari Bedekar's 1948 misal anchor, now run by the third generation. The Puneri style is yellow-broth (turmeric-cumin base, less chilli than Kolhapur, no coconut) topped with kand-bhel — the version every other Pune misal house copies.
insider_tip: Single misal serving size only — no double portions. The 'tarri' (oil-floating broth) is poured at table; ask for 'extra tarri' once on a fresh batch. Closed Wednesdays (notable — most Pune locals get caught). Cash + UPI; no cards.
signature_address: 425, Narayan Peth, near Bharat Natya Mandir, Pune 411030

name: Ramnath Hotel (Misal)
why_it_matters: Shantilal Khanna's no-frills 60-year-old misal shop in Khadki Bazaar — the red-tarri (fiery oil) version that Pune purists prefer to Bedekar's yellow. Workers' canteen energy: plastic chairs, single dish, breakfast-only.
insider_tip: Opens 6.30am, runs out by 11am — go before 9am. The 'extra tarri' is the move (locals dunk pav and refill twice). Cash only. Sundays drawn the longest queue.

name: Sujata Mastani
why_it_matters: Pune-original Mastani is a thick mawa-milk kulfi-shake named after Bajirao I's mistress — Sujata's 1958 Sadashiv Peth flagship is the city anchor for it. Pistachio is the signature, fresh-ground daily, not paste. Multiple branches now, but the SP shop is the original.
insider_tip: Best 5-9pm; April-May queues hit 30 minutes. Mango mastani is May-June seasonal only. Cash + UPI; no cards. Sit-down at the SP shop; takeaway at the other branches.
signature_address: 1306, Sadashiv Peth, near Tilak Road, Pune 411030

name: Kayani Bakery
why_it_matters: Khodayar Irani's 70-year-old Camp bakery — the Shrewsbury biscuit (a Pune-original buttery shortbread named after the English town) is the souvenir Pune Instagram won't shut up about. Mawa cakes baked fresh daily at 4pm.
insider_tip: Shrewsbury biscuits at ~₹600/kg sell out by 11am — go right after the 8.30am opening. Mawa-cake batch lands 4pm Mon-Sat; queue starts 3.45pm. Cash only, no UPI (the legend). Closed Sundays. Limit 5 tins per customer on weekends.

name: German Bakery
why_it_matters: Robert Stutz's 1989 Lane 7 cafe — the Osho-ashram backpacker default. On 13 February 2010 a bomb killed 17; the bakery reopened 1 July 2013 at the same address, same name, as a deliberate act of remembrance with a memorial wall inside listing the names.
insider_tip: Breakfast 7-11am is quietest (Osho meditators come 11.30am+). Sourdough loaves sell out by 2pm Sat-Sun. Cards + UPI accepted; the memorial wall is on the left as you enter.
signature_address: North Main Road, Lane 7, Koregaon Park, Pune 411001

name: Cafe Goodluck
why_it_matters: Hussain Ali Yakhshi's 1935 cafe — Pune's oldest Irani establishment, where bun maska and Irani chai have been served on the same Deccan Gymkhana corner for 90 years. The wooden chairs, ceiling fans and Bombay-blue walls are unchanged.
insider_tip: The corner booth near the entrance is the prize seat. Bun maska is fresher in the morning (7-10am); kheema pav is the lunch order. Cash + UPI.
signature_address: Opposite Goodluck Chowk, FC Road, Deccan Gymkhana, Pune 411004

name: Dorabjee & Sons
why_it_matters: Pune's oldest Parsi restaurant — 148 years on Dastur Meher Road, now run by the fourth Dorabjee generation. Sunday dhansak is the city ritual; the chicken farcha (egg-and-breadcrumb-fried chicken) is the everyday order.
insider_tip: Sunday lunch 12-3pm sees 30-minute queues — go weekday for the same dhansak no wait. Closed Mondays. The first-floor seating is calmer than the ground-floor. Cash + cards.
signature_address: 1, Dastur Meher Road, near Sarbatwala Chowk, Camp, Pune 411001

name: Marz-O-Rin
why_it_matters: MG Road institution since 1965, set inside the 125-year-old Bakhtiar Building. The chutney sandwich and thick mango milkshake have been the post-shopping ritual for generations of Punekars. First-date venue, last-minute snack, no menu changes since the 70s.
insider_tip: Counter-service only — order at the front, wait for your token to be called. Mango milkshake is fresh-fruit, summer-best (Apr-Jun). Cash + UPI.
signature_address: Bakhtiar Building, MG Road, Camp, Pune 411001

name: Shabree
why_it_matters: Pune's reference Maharashtrian thali — thalipith, sabudana, bharleli vangi, varan-bhaat, aamti, shrikhand on a single brass plate. Hotel Parichay's restaurant arm; the thali is unlimited and refilled by waiters in traditional dhoti-kurta.
insider_tip: Lunch 12-3.30pm is the better meal — fresh thalipith straight off the tava. Reserve on weekends (60-minute waits otherwise). The mahaprasad seasonal thali (Ganesh Chaturthi + Diwali) is genuinely special.
signature_address: Hotel Parichay, Apte Road, Deccan Gymkhana, Pune 411004

name: Wadeshwar
why_it_matters: Pune's 50-year-old South Indian–Maharashtrian chain that started on FC Road. The kothimbir vadi (coriander-besan steamed cake) and thalipith here are the city benchmark. Now 7+ outlets across Pune; the FC Road flagship is the original.
insider_tip: Breakfast 7.30-10.30am is the calmest — dosas straight off the tava. Cards + UPI accepted; AC seating upstairs. The Baner and Kalyani Nagar outlets are equally consistent if FC Road queue is too long.
signature_address: Fergusson College Road, near Goodluck Cafe, Pune 411004

name: Joshi Wadewale
why_it_matters: Vasant Joshi's 1974 vada-pav cart, now an 8-outlet local chain. The original JM Road shop sells 3,000+ vadas a day — sun-bright yellow garlic chutney is the differentiator. Pune's reference for the dish.
insider_tip: Fresh vadas drop every 20 minutes; ask the counter when the next batch comes. The dry red garlic chutney (lasoon chutney) is the secret. Cash + UPI.
signature_address: 1281, Jangali Maharaj Road, Shivaji Nagar, Pune 411005

name: Malaka Spice
why_it_matters: Praful and Cheeru Chandawarkar's 1997 garden-restaurant in KP — Pune's first proper Southeast Asian kitchen, with an outdoor seating wall covered in graffiti. The Burmese khao suey here is the Pune reference. Now 3 outlets (KP, Kharadi, Amanora); the KP original is the one.
insider_tip: Garden seating is the move (rain-cover available monsoon). Lunch is calmer than dinner; the lunch set menu is half the dinner cost. Cards + UPI. Reserve weekends.
signature_address: Lane 5, Koregaon Park, near North Main Road, Pune 411001

name: Effingut Brewerkz
why_it_matters: Pune's first proper microbrewery and the city's craft-beer anchor — 12 taps including unfiltered hefeweizen, mango-chilli cider, choco-coffee stout, plus 5-6 seasonal beers. Pune is widely regarded as India's craft-beer epicentre alongside Bangalore; Effingut led the wave.
insider_tip: Tasting flight (5 beers × 100ml = ₹450) is the right first move. Live music Thursday-Saturday from 8pm. The KP location has the best outdoor seating; Kharadi outlet has more taps. Cards only; no cash.
signature_address: Plot 13, Koregaon Park Annex, near Osho Garden, Pune 411001

name: Independence Brewing Company
why_it_matters: Pune's most-awarded microbrewery, Mundhwa location set in a converted warehouse — Summer Blonde Ale and Four Grain Saison are the flagships, Honey Lavender Ale is the room's signature. Open warehouse ceilings, exposed beams, 200+ seats.
insider_tip: Lunch is 50% less crowded than dinner. The brewery tour (₹500, weekends only at 4pm) is a real walk-through of the mash tun. Live music Friday + Saturday from 9pm. Cards + UPI.

name: Blue Nile
why_it_matters: Camp's reliable Mughlai-biryani anchor for 45 years — mutton dum biryani served in copper pots, scaled to feed Pune Cantonment's late-night army crowd. The pre-pour gravy on top is the move.
insider_tip: Open till 1am — the post-bar biryani run. Half-plate mutton biryani feeds one comfortably; full plate splits between two. Cash + UPI; no cards.
signature_address: 16, Mahatma Gandhi Road, opposite Victory Theatre, Camp, Pune 411001

name: Nisarga
why_it_matters: Pune's original Malvani seafood house, predating Mahesh and Gajalee's local branches by a decade. Bombil fry and surmai are flown in daily from Ratnagiri; the sol-kadhi (kokum-coconut buttermilk) is the table-side coolant.
insider_tip: Ask for the daily fish board (chalkboard inside) — bangda, paplet, surmai availability changes. Lunch is when the fish is freshest. Cards + UPI.
signature_address: Tilak Road, near Sadashiv Peth junction, Pune 411030

name: Sweekar
why_it_matters: A no-frills Maharashtrian thali house off Bajirao Road that office crowds and Tilak Road shoppers clear at lunch. Unlimited bhakri and amti for under ₹300 — the value bar for Maharashtrian food in central Pune.
insider_tip: Lunch 12-3.30pm only — no dinner. Closed Sundays. Arrive 12.15pm for hot bhakri straight off the tava; by 2pm refills slow. Cash only.
signature_address: Bajirao Road, near Tilak Road junction, Sadashiv Peth, Pune 411030
